title: Elasticsearch: every Wikipedia page is parsed and indexed
summary: Parses the Wikipedia HTML pages, chunks them and loads them into the Elasticsearch index wiki_pages, then checks the job was clean and every page is present. Known defect: Optical_fiber.html fails to parse, so this scenario is expected to fail and show which page is missing.

steps.title: Delete the wiki_pages index
steps.explain: Starts from a clean slate so every document found later was written by this run.

steps.title: List the source HTML pages
steps.explain: The pages a correct run must index.

steps.title: Count documents in the index (Before)
steps.explain: Before the run the index does not exist, so it holds nothing.

steps.title: Run the es_wiki_pages pipeline
steps.explain: Runs the real pipeline. Everything below checks what it produced.

steps.title: Job finished with status COMPLETED
steps.explain: PARTIAL means some part of the work failed.

steps.title: Job reported 0 warnings
steps.explain: Each warning is a page or step that went wrong.

steps.title: No warning or error lines in the output
steps.explain: Shows the actual warning text the job printed, if any.

steps.title: Count documents in the index (After)
steps.explain: The real number of chunks Elasticsearch holds.

steps.title: The index holds documents
steps.explain: An empty index would mean nothing was loaded.

steps.title: List the distinct pages in the index
steps.explain: Which source pages made it into the index.

steps.title: Every source page is in the index
steps.explain: Names any page that was read but did not arrive.
